question: For Windows `install.ps1` npm certificate failures, should OpenClaw offer explicit CA/cafile remediation only, a prompted `--strict-ssl=false` break-glass fallback, or diagnostic guidance without an automated fallback?
rationale: The affected code path is narrow, but the acceptable recovery changes the installer TLS trust boundary and cannot be safely chosen by automation.

options.title: Prefer explicit CA remediation
options.body: Detect npm TLS certificate failures, keep strict verification on by default, and guide or apply an operator-approved `cafile`/`NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` remediation with clear proof.

options.title: Allow prompted break-glass retry
options.body: Permit a clearly warned interactive `--strict-ssl=false` retry only when maintainers accept the installer MITM tradeoff for blocked Windows users.

options.title: Diagnostics only
options.body: Improve the error and docs but leave certificate-store repair to the user or enterprise environment, preserving strict installer trust at the cost of first-run recovery.

recommendation.title: Prefer explicit CA remediation
recommendation.body: Detect npm TLS certificate failures, keep strict verification on by default, and guide or apply an operator-approved `cafile`/`NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` remediation with clear proof.
